essentials.label: Audit
essentials.title: PROGRESS OF ACTION IDENTIFIED IN THE ANNUAL GOVERNANCE STATEMENT 2025-26

news_drafts.headline: South Derbyshire's audit team faces staffing pressures with recommendations from 2021/22 unresolved
news_drafts.lead: South Derbyshire Council's internal audit team is managing staffing pressure by using external associates to fill gaps, rather than more costly agency staff. Onboarding these associates has proved lengthy, with the council facing challenges around gaining system access for the new team members. Eight audits were completed this year with 24 recommendations made. Yet audit recommendations from 2021/22 remain unresolved, with the internal auditor referring to moderate and low-risk issues with the council's controls and procedures from these earlier audits still being outstanding. These represent actions, the auditor confirmed, that management continues to work on.

findings.headline: Beyond three-year settlement to 2028/29, material uncertainty over funding from Fair Funding Review and business rates reset not yet detailed by government
findings.detail: The council operates under a three-year local government funding settlement announced February 2026, providing certainty to 2028/29. Beyond that point, the MTFP for 2029/30-2030/31 relies on assumptions from specialist advisors (Pixel Financial) because the Fair Funding Review reforms and business rates baseline reset are still being designed by government. The council's planning assumes funding may not increase in line with inflation and demand growth. It notes that 'changes to national distribution methodologies could materially affect the Council's resources', creating material planning uncertainty in the final two years covered by the MTFP.
findings.matters: Multi-year settlements provide planning certainty; loss of that certainty beyond year 3 creates long-term planning risk. If future funding falls short of assumptions, the council faces urgent deficits at a point when capacity to respond is constrained by the new unitary structure.
findings.figures: Three-year settlement to 2028/29; MTFP extends to 2030/31 with uncertain funding beyond 2028/29
findings.quote: Beyond the three-year Local Government Finance Settlement period to 2028/29, there remains a significant degree of uncertainty over the level and distribution of local government funding.

findings.headline: 2027/28 is final year of independent budget-setting before merger into unitary authority on 1 April 2028; decisions must avoid creating financial liabilities for successor
findings.detail: The council faces reorganisation into a new unitary authority with vesting on 1 April 2028. This makes 2027/28 the final year for sovereign budget-setting. The report frames decisions as carrying 'dual responsibility': balancing current service delivery with the imperative to avoid creating preventable financial pressures for the new authority. Budget-setting principles explicitly require proposals to 'avoid unnecessary future commitments' and 'leave a strong position for the new authority'. This creates a governance tension between responding to current needs and financial stewardship for the transition.
findings.matters: Mergers create organizational risk and final-year budget cycles often see service deterioration, control erosion, or unfunded liabilities passed forward. How well a council manages this tension is material to the resilience of the successor authority.
findings.figures: Vesting date 1 April 2028; 2027/28 is final sovereign budget-setting year
findings.quote: 2027/28 is the final year of sovereign budget setting ahead of local government reorganisation. Every decision carries a dual responsibility, therefore the Council has to balance meeting the needs of our residents, while maintaining a sustainable financial position.

findings.headline: £14.1m Sustainable Finance Programme scheduled over five years with only £630k delivered to date; delivery risk elevated by local government reorganisation
findings.detail: The council's five-theme Sustainable Finance Programme targets £14.1m cumulative savings and income over 2026/27-2030/31, with commercial/income opportunities accounting for £9.9m (the largest element). Only £630k has been achieved or included in the 2026/27 budget, leaving £13.5m for future years. The programme timeline has been reshaped by local government reorganisation, with unitary vesting planned for April 2028. The report notes that reorganisation creates capacity pressures, implementation costs, and structural uncertainty that affect both timing and deliverability of the remaining £13.5m.
findings.matters: The council is dependent on realizing substantial future savings. Delivery risk is acute because the majority of the programme is scheduled for years 2027-2031 (the same period as the merger transition), meaning competing demands on officer capacity at the point when savings are most critical.
findings.figures: £14.1m total programme target; £630k achieved/in budget 2026/27; £13.5m future delivery required; commercial/income £9.9m, transformation £771k, asset management £594k, managing spend £1.2m, treasury £1.0m
findings.quote: Local Government Reorganisation, with vesting day anticipated in April 2028, is reshaping the SFP's planning horizon and delivery priorities. The programme must support both continued financial sustainability and a stable financial legacy for the new Unitary Council.

findings.headline: Budget Optimisation Board delivered £1.66m of savings for 2026/27 through service reviews, vacancy management, and commercial income
findings.detail: The Board identified and delivered £1.655m in savings: service development reviews (£351k), vacancy savings (£253k), commercial income (£258k), and new opportunities (£795k). The Board is continuing to play a critical role for 2027/28, focusing initially on opportunities identified in the 2026/27 process but held pending political direction, plus new opportunities to be identified during the budget setting process.
findings.matters: Demonstrates the council's ability to locate and deliver savings when facing budget pressures, and indicates whether the savings base is sustainable or dependent on non-recurring opportunities such as vacancies.
findings.figures: Total £1,655,766 comprising: service reviews £350,557; vacancies £252,615; commercial income £257,972; new opportunities £794,622
findings.quote: £1.65 million of savings delivered to address the predicted budget gap for 2026/27. As a result, the budget for 2026/27 out turned a balanced budget position.

findings.headline: First-quarter 2026/27 forecast shows £227k deficit versus £634 budgeted, with service overspends offset by higher planning income
findings.detail: At Q1, the council forecasted a full-year deficit of £227,134 compared to the £634 budgeted, a variance of £226,500. The overshoot reflects service expenditure pressures being partially offset by additional planning income above budget. This in-year pressure triggered the need for corrective action by the Budget Optimisation Board. The revised MTFP subsequently shows a £102,635 position for the year, suggesting further adjustments have been factored in.
findings.matters: Early-year variances indicate whether budget assumptions about service costs and income are realistic. Persistent service overspends signal structural spending pressures that savings programmes must address.
findings.figures: Q1 forecast deficit £227,134 vs budget £634; variance £226,500; revised full-year forecast £102,635
findings.quote: The current forecast position on the General fund for 2026/27 is a deficit for the year of £227,134 compared to a budgeted deficit position of £634. The main variations to budget are overspends in service expenditure, being offset by additional planning income.
